summary: The service/route/schema layer for the 5 phase_8 gap items (prompt translation, localization, marketplace, export, import) is well-architected -- it correctly extends the existing Prompt Operating System, gates every mutating action through requirePromptPermissionForUser()/veridian_admin, uses requireAuth() on every route, avoids XSS via normal JSX escaping, caches LLM calls by (version, locale) to avoid re-translating, and validates/deduplicates import bundles inside a transaction. However, the new migration drizzle/0268_prompt_translation_localization_marketplace.sql creates 3 new tables (prompt_translations, prompt_localizations, prompt_marketplace_listings) with no ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, no CREATE POLICY, and no GRANT statements at all -- a clear deviation from every sibling migration in this same task batch (drizzle/0266 and drizzle/0267, both also new-table migrations opened in this same PR wave) and from the precedent this PR's own migration comment claims to follow (compliance.prompt_templates/prompt_versions in drizzle/0019, which -- despite being platform-wide, non-tenant data exactly like these new tables -- still explicitly GRANTs SELECT/INSERT to app_runtime and SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE to service_role). Confirmed via drizzle/0008's ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES that only service_role gets schema-wide default grants; app_runtime (the role Drizzle's DATABASE_URL connection uses for every other table in this codebase) gets nothing by default and requires an explicit per-table GRANT, which this migration omits. Net effect: once the supervising session applies this migration as-is, every one of the 5 new API routes (translate/localize/export/import/marketplace) will fail with a Postgres permission-denied error the first time app_runtime tries to read or write these tables, because the migration is not applied live and this is invisible to the mocked-DB unit tests and tsc, this real, significant defect will not surface until production. This needs a fix (add ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY + a real or intentionally-omitted read policy, matching the platform-wide-no-tenant-scope pattern, + explicit GRANT to app_runtime and service_role) before this is safe to hand to the human for sign-off/merge.
issues: drizzle/0268_prompt_translation_localization_marketplace.sql: none of the 3 new tables (prompt_translations, prompt_localizations, prompt_marketplace_listings) have ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, CREATE POLICY, or GRANT statements, unlike every sibling new-table migration in this repo (drizzle/0266, drizzle/0267) and the platform-wide prompt_templates/prompt_versions precedent this migration's own header comment claims to follow (drizzle/0019, which does GRANT SELECT/INSERT to app_runtime despite also being non-tenant-scoped data). Since app_runtime has no schema-wide default privileges (only service_role does, per drizzle/0008's ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES), the Drizzle app connection will get a permission-denied error on every read/write to these 3 tables once this migration is applied live -- breaking all 5 new API routes in production. Needs GRANT (+ RLS enable/policy, consistent with the platform-wide posture) added before this migration is safe to apply.
